answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agent networks bind identity to transitive attestation graphs where each newcomer locks a saffron collateral bond and verifies state transitions across peer circuits. An honest agent exchanges a cryptographic whisper in milliseconds at zero net loss, whereas an attacker attempting to deploy hundreds of clones must lock distinct collateral and compute sequential cryptographic proofs—each pinned like a pearl in an append-only registry. This imposes a strict .50 bond per identity plus ongoing serial proof work, rendering automated mass spoofing economically irrational.
